questions.stem: About the skeleton of the thoracic limb:
options: The shoulder girdle is formed by the scapula and the clavicle
The forearm skeleton is formed by the radius laterally and the ulna medially
It is attached to the thorax by the shoulder girdle
The shoulder girdle is formed by the scapula and the humerus
The humerus alone forms the skeleton of the arm
questions.explanation: The shoulder girdle = scapula + clavicle (paired bones); the humerus is the arm skeleton.

questions.stem: The clavicle:
options: Has a deep, non-palpable superior surface
Is a long bone shaped like an extended "S"
Extends between the scapula and the humerus
Has a posterior border that is convex in its lateral 1/3
Has an anterior border that is concave in its medial 2/3
questions.explanation: The anterior border is concave in its lateral 1/3 and convex in its medial 2/3; the posterior border is the reverse (convex lateral 1/3, concave medial 2/3). Also false: "Extends between the scapula and the humerus"; "Has a deep, non-palpable superior surface".

questions.stem: On the inferior surface of the clavicle, which structure gives attachment to the costoclavicular ligament?
options: The acromial articular surface
The conoid tubercle
The groove for the subclavius
The costal tuberosity
The trapezoid line
questions.explanation: Medially, the costal tuberosity (costoclavicular ligament); in the middle, the subclavius groove; laterally, trapezoid line and conoid tubercle (coracoclavicular ligament: trapezoid and conoid parts).

questions.stem: About the extremities of the clavicle:
options: The sternal end articulates with the first rib only
The acromial end articulates with the acromion of the scapula
The acromial end is medial and rounded
The sternal end articulates with the coracoid process
The sternal end is medial and rounded
questions.explanation: The sternal end articulates with the sternum and 1st costal cartilage; the coracoid process is linked to the clavicle by ligaments, not a joint surface. Also false: "The acromial end is medial and rounded"; "The sternal end articulates with the first rib only".

questions.stem: The scapula:
options: Is a flat, triangular, dorsal bone
Is oriented with its concave surface backward
Projects between the 1st and the 10th ribs
Articulates with the humerus and the clavicle
Projects between the 2nd and the 7th ribs
questions.explanation: The scapula projects onto the 2nd rib above and the 7th rib below; its concave (costal) surface faces forward.

questions.stem: About the faces of the scapula:
options: The scapular spine extends laterally as the coracoid process
The anterior surface forms the subscapular fossa for the subscapularis
The supraspinous fossa gives insertion to the subscapularis
The posterior surface is divided by the scapular spine into supraspinous and infraspinous fossae
The infraspinous fossa gives insertion to the infraspinatus, teres minor and teres major
questions.explanation: The supraspinous fossa receives the supraspinatus; the spine extends laterally as the acromion, which carries the clavicular articular surface.

questions.stem: The scapular notch:
options: Is surmounted by the transverse ligament of the scapula
Is on the lateral angle
Gives passage to the suprascapular artery and nerve
Gives passage to the radial nerve
Is on the superior (cervical) border
questions.explanation: The scapular notch belongs to the superior border, not the lateral angle (a classic exam trap).

questions.stem: About the lateral angle of the scapula:
options: The supraglenoid tubercle gives insertion to the long head of triceps
The neck of the scapula supports the glenoid cavity
The infraglenoid tubercle gives insertion to the long head of biceps
The glenoid cavity is oval, notched anteriorly, with the glenoid tubercle at its centre
The coracoid process gives insertion to the short head of biceps, coracobrachialis and pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: It is reversed: supraglenoid tubercle = long head of biceps; infraglenoid tubercle = long head of triceps.

questions.stem: About the diaphysis of the humerus:
options: It is cylindrical above and triangular and flattened below
The radial nerve groove crosses its posterior surface
The lateral head of triceps inserts below the radial groove
The crest of the greater tubercle gives insertion to the latissimus dorsi
The deltoid tuberosity is on its anterolateral surface
questions.explanation: Lateral head of triceps above the groove, medial head below. The crest of the greater tubercle (anterior border) receives the pectoralis major; latissimus dorsi inserts on the crest of the lesser tubercle.

questions.stem: A fracture of the middle of the humeral shaft causes wrist drop. Which structure on the humerus explains this?
options: The surgical neck
The groove for the ulnar nerve on the medial epicondyle
The intertubercular groove
The radial nerve groove on the posterior surface
The deltoid tuberosity
questions.explanation: The radial nerve runs in the radial nerve groove on the posterior surface of the humeral shaft, so it can be injured in shaft fractures.

questions.stem: About the proximal epiphysis of the humerus:
options: The surgical neck separates the proximal epiphysis from the diaphysis and is vulnerable to fractures
The anatomical neck separates the proximal epiphysis from the diaphysis
The lesser tubercle is a large lateral projection
The humeral head represents 2/3 of a sphere
The intertubercular groove gives passage to the tendon of the long head of biceps
questions.explanation: The greater tubercle is the large lateral projection; the lesser tubercle is a small anterior projection. Also false: "The humeral head represents 2/3 of a sphere"; "The anatomical neck separates the proximal epiphysis from the diaphysis".

questions.stem: About the humeral condyle:
options: The capitulum is lateral, rounded and not visible from behind
The trochlea is medial and articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna
The capitulum articulates with the radial head
The olecranon fossa lies anteriorly above the trochlea
The trochlea is surmounted by the radial fossa
questions.explanation: The capitulum is surmounted by the radial fossa; the trochlea by the coronoid fossa (anteriorly) and the olecranon fossa (posteriorly).

questions.stem: The medial epicondyle of the humerus:
options: Gives attachment to the radial collateral ligament
Is poorly developed
Is crossed posteriorly by the groove for the ulnar nerve
Gives attachment to the ulnar collateral ligament of the elbow
Is very developed and palpable
questions.explanation: The lateral epicondyle is the poorly developed one, giving attachment to the radial collateral ligament.

questions.stem: About the ulna:
options: It is the medial bone of the forearm
The coronoid process is horizontal and anterior
Its medial border is the interosseous border
The olecranon is horizontal and anterior
The radial notch is on the medial surface of the coronoid process
questions.explanation: The radial notch of the ulna is on the lateral (outer) side of the coronoid process, articulating with the radial articular circumference. Also false: "Its medial border is the interosseous border"; "The olecranon is horizontal and anterior".

questions.stem: Which muscle inserts on the ulnar tuberosity?
options: The biceps brachii
The brachialis
The triceps brachii
The brachioradialis
The coracobrachialis
questions.explanation: The ulnar tuberosity, in front of the coronoid process, receives the brachialis. The biceps ends on the radial tuberosity; triceps on the olecranon.

questions.stem: About the distal epiphysis of the ulna:
options: The ulnar head articulates with the radioulnar articular disc
The ulnar styloid process is a large anterolateral projection
The ulnar head articulates directly with the lunate
The ulnar styloid process gives attachment to the radial collateral ligament of the carpus
The ulnar head articulates with the ulnar notch of the radius
questions.explanation: The ulna does not articulate directly with the carpus: the radioulnar articular disc is interposed. Also false: "The ulnar styloid process is a large anterolateral projection"; "The ulnar styloid process gives attachment to the radial collateral ligament of the carpus".

questions.stem: About the proximal epiphysis of the radius:
options: The articular circumference articulates with the radial notch of the ulna and the annular ligament
The fovea articulates with the radial notch of the ulna
The articular circumference articulates with the capitulum
The radial articular fovea is superior and concave
The radial tuberosity receives the termination of the brachialis
questions.explanation: The fovea (cupula) faces the capitulum; the peripheral circumference faces the ulna's radial notch and the annular ligament. Also false: "The fovea articulates with the radial notch of the ulna"; "The radial tuberosity receives the termination of the brachialis".

questions.stem: About the distal epiphysis of the radius:
options: Its lateral surface extends down as the radial styloid process
It is a quadrangular pyramid with an inferior base
Its lateral surface carries the ulnar notch
Its posterior surface is smooth
Its anterior surface has two grooves for seven tendons
questions.explanation: It is the posterior surface that is furrowed (2 grooves, 7 tendons); the lateral surface's styloid is bordered by 2 grooves for 3 tendons. Also false: "Its anterior surface has two grooves for seven tendons"; "Its lateral surface carries the ulnar notch".

questions.stem: Which carpal bones form the proximal row (from lateral to medial)?
options: Scaphoid
Pisiform
Trapezium
Lunate
Triquetrum
questions.explanation: Proximal row: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform. Distal row: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

questions.stem: This palmar view of a right carpus shows the carpal bones numbered 1 to 8. Which identifications are correct?
options: 7 is the hamate
1 is the scaphoid
4 is the pisiform
5 is the trapezoid
2 is the lunate
questions.explanation: Proximal row lateral→medial: 1 scaphoid, 2 lunate, 3 triquetrum, 4 pisiform. Distal row: 5 trapezium, 6 trapezoid, 7 capitate, 8 hamate.

questions.stem: The carpal tunnel:
options: Gives passage to muscle tendons
Is on the posterior face of the carpus
Gives passage to the radial nerve
Is formed by the carpal groove completed by the flexor retinaculum
Gives passage to the median nerve
questions.explanation: The anterior (palmar) face of the carpus is concave (carpal groove); with the flexor retinaculum it forms the carpal tunnel for the median nerve and tendons.

questions.stem: About the metacarpus and phalanges:
options: There are 5 metacarpals numbered I to V from lateral to medial
There are 14 phalanges
The thumb has 2 phalanges
The thumb has 3 phalanges
The base is the distal end of a phalanx
questions.explanation: Each phalanx has a proximal base and a distal head. The thumb has 2 phalanges (P1, P2), the other fingers 3.

questions.stem: Bone age in a child is assessed on:
options: A CT scan of the skull
An X-ray of the right foot
An X-ray of the left wrist and hand
An MRI of the knee
An X-ray of the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Bone age is assessed on an X-ray of the left wrist and hand (ossification of the carpal bones and of the epiphyses of the wrist/hand long bones).
